title: AI Literacy for the Modern Workplace
description: Many workplaces are telling people to use artificial intelligence before explaining what good use looks like. AI Literacy for the Modern Workplace fixes that gap. Written in plain English for managers, team leaders, HR, operations staff, knowledge workers and non-technical professionals, it explains the practical literacy people need to use AI sensibly at work. This is not a coding book and not a glossy innovation brochure. It covers what AI can and cannot do, how to write better prompts, how to check outputs, where human judgement matters, what data should be protected, how teams should set rules and how managers can encourage useful adoption without creating chaos. The book also deals with awkward questions: job anxiety, over-reliance, bias, accuracy, accountability, policy and the difference between productivity and simply producing more stuff. The aim is straightforward: help teams become confident, careful and useful AI users, not passengers in someone else’s software experiment.
short_description: A practical workplace guide to AI literacy for managers, teams and non-technical professionals, covering prompts, policy, risk and judgement.
author: Jonathan Harris
audience: Managers, team leaders, HR professionals, operations staff, knowledge workers, administrators and non-technical professionals who need practical AI confidence at work.
